**The cabled grade** — phase 9.
Described by `906`.

## What it publishes

| symbol | unit | kind | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_pair_spout` | 1 | given | 512 | differential pairs the cabled grade uses. Two thousand was the first figure and draws two hundred and sixty watts, which is three times even the transient port allowance -- a serial link costs picojoules a bit where a ten micron bond costs femtojoules, and that is the real reason this grade is narrow |
| `r_pair_spout` | bit/s | given | 3.2e+10 bit/s | rate one pair carries |
| `n_mate_cycle` | 1 | given | 200 | mating cycles the connector is rated for |
| `L_cable_spout` | mm | given | 1000 mm | reach |
| `e_ser_bit` | pJ/bit | measured | 4 pJ/bit | energy a bit costs over this link, both ends and the serialiser included |
| `B_cabled` | bit/s | derived | 1.6384e+13 bit/s | what the cabled grade carries |
| `ratio_bonded` | 1 | derived | 1024 | how much narrower it is than the bonded grade |
| `ratio_net_c` | 1 | derived | 40.96 | and how much wider than a network interface |
| `t_pane_ser` | s | derived | 1.024e-06 s | how long one pane takes to serialise, which is what makes it not the same thing arriving |
| `t_core_out_c` | s | derived | 0.0351296 s | whole-core transfer time on this grade |
| `P_cabled` | W | derived | 65.536 W | what it costs while running |
| `n_pad_spout_c` | 1 | derived | 1024 | perimeter positions it needs |

## What it consumes

| symbol | from | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `B_spout_burst` | `062` | 1.67772e+16 bit/s | the burst rate as a bandwidth |
| `C_core_usable` | `034` | 71.9454 GB | what a model may actually use |
| `L_reach_line` | `057` | 3000 mm | reach of the adopted serial standard at this rate, from its own specification |
| `P_port_burst` | `020` | 80 W | what the port fields may draw transiently: a model load runs the storage lines flat out for tens of milliseconds, and the spout's pane costs more again for microseconds. Neither is in the steady budget and 026 is where both are absorbed |
| `n_pad_perim` | `056` | 6400 | positions in the perimeter zone |
| `n_pane_bit` | `062` | 1.67772e+07 bit | the pane, rounded down to a power of two so that its window aligns naturally in 038. It carries the unit because it is a quantity of bits rather than a count of things, and everything downstream of it is a size or a rate |
| `n_port_conductor` | `056` | 256 | conductors that must reach the interposer through 014's via islands |
| `r_net_ref` | `062` | 4e+11 bit/s | a fast network interface, as the comparison everybody will make |
| `t_pane_empty` | `062` | 1e-09 s | how long the spout takes to empty it |

## What it asserts

| tag | relation | because |
|---|---|---|
| `C-067-1` | `n_pad_spout_c + n_port_conductor <= n_pad_perim` | the pairs and the power must both fit the perimeter zone, since this grade shares it with the face's own supply |
| `C-067-2` | `ratio_bonded > 100` | this grade is two orders of magnitude narrower than the bonded one. Asserted so the comparison is in the record rather than left for somebody to be disappointed by |
| `C-067-3` | `ratio_net_c > 10` | and more than an order of magnitude wider than a network interface. Both comparisons, because either alone misleads |
| `C-067-4` | `P_cabled < P_port_burst` | it must fit inside the transient port allowance while it runs |
| `C-067-5` | `t_pane_ser > t_pane_empty * 100` | serialising a pane takes far longer than emitting one, which is the arithmetic behind saying the cube-side interface cannot be identical -- and therefore behind moving that requirement to the core side |
| `C-067-6` | `L_cable_spout < L_reach_line` | the cable must be inside the reach of the standard adopted for it |
